summary.title: PyGoat CI/CD pipeline
summary.description: Supply-chain threat model: GitHub Actions scan, release (cosign + SBOM) and deploy pipeline for PyGoat. Threats: tutor-written study model (2026-11-08) except the two marked 'Reasoned by the student'. Facts checked via gh api and the workflow files.

data.name: CI scan jobs
data.description: Runners for flake8, hadolint, Semgrep, gitleaks, Sonar, Snyk on PRs and pushes

threats.title: A third-party action is swapped for malicious code
threats.description: Who: whoever compromises an action's repository (e.g. tj-actions/changed-files, March 2025). How: a version tag like @v4 is moved to a malicious commit; every workflow using the tag runs it. Harmed: everything the job can reach - code, tokens, artifacts.
threats.mitigation: Mitigated: every 'uses:' is pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA (checked 2026-11-08; fix 5f45b6b, PLANTED.md #1). Keep current with Dependabot/Renovate PRs that update the SHA.

threats.title: Scanner gate skipped or made to pass
threats.description: Who: a collaborator. How: edits a scan workflow (add continue-on-error, narrow the paths, --soft-fail) in the same PR as the risky code; the gate goes green on code it never really checked. Harmed: every later stage trusts a meaningless green.
threats.mitigation: Prevent: enforce CODEOWNERS review on /.github/ and keep the scan checks in the ruleset's required_status_checks. Detect: review diffs to workflow files as security changes.

data.name: Release job
data.description: On master: build image, push, sign with cosign, attach SBOM

threats.title: Release job token can publish anything to GHCR
threats.description: Who: anyone who gets code into master. How: release.yml has packages: write and id-token: write; whatever is on master is built, pushed and signed as if trusted. Harmed: the registry - a malicious image gets a valid signature, because the signature proves where it was built, not that the code is good.
threats.mitigation: Prevent: protect master (see Git repository threat); keep permissions per job, not workflow-wide; production environment approval before deploy (production has required_reviewers). Know the limit: cosign proves provenance, not safety.

threats.title: Part of DEPLOY_TOKEN printed to public logs
threats.description: Who: anyone - the repo is public, so its Actions logs are readable by everyone. How: deploy.yml echoes "token starts with: ${DEPLOY_TOKEN%%-*}"; GitHub masks the whole secret, not a piece of it. Harmed: part of a production credential is public, which shrinks what is left to guess and may reveal the token type/issuer. [Reasoned by the student 2026-11-08.]
threats.mitigation: Prevent: remove the echo; never print any part of a secret. Respond: rotate DEPLOY_TOKEN now (it has been in public logs). Better: replace the static token with OIDC to the cloud, so there is no long-lived secret at all.

data.name: Git repository
data.description: Source code and the workflow files themselves

threats.title: Code reaches master without a second person
threats.description: Who: any collaborator, or the repo admin. How: the require-pr ruleset (no deletion, no force-push, PR + required checks) needs 0 approvals, and RepositoryRole can bypass it; a single account can merge its own change. Harmed: integrity of master, which feeds the release and deploy.
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: ruleset 'require-pr' active on the default branch (blocks force-push and deletion, requires checks). Ticket: 1 required approval + code-owner review once there is a second maintainer; remove or log bypass; require signed commits.

threats.title: Image is public
threats.description: Who: anyone. How: the GHCR package visibility is public. Harmed: anyone can pull and inspect the image - which is intended for this open-source training app.
threats.mitigation: Accepted/by design for an open-source app: no secrets are baked into the image (gitleaks + Trivy scan it). A private app would set the package to private.

threats.title: Fork PR code runs with secrets (pull_request_target)
threats.description: Who: anyone on GitHub. How: pr-check.yml used pull_request_target and checked out the fork's code, running untrusted code in the base repo's context with a secret (PLANTED.md #11, J00). Harmed: repository secrets and write token.
threats.mitigation: Mitigated: switched to pull_request (pr-check.yml:4), fix e949c50; proven red 37241098182 -> green 37242094519 in J00. Fork PRs now run without secrets, outside Box B.

threats.title: Scan tokens stolen by code running in CI
threats.description:
Who: anyone with write access to the repo, a stolen collaborator account or token, or a compromised Action or dependency. Fork PRs don't get secrets unless a workflow uses pull_request_target.
How: a branch PR or push edits a workflow or a script the job runs, or adds a malicious package, so the job sends the token somewhere or prints it base64-encoded.
Harmed: with the tokens, an attacker can fake a passing quality gate, read SonarCloud results and code, see unpatched vulnerabilities in Snyk, and mute findings.
threats.mitigation:
GitHub withholds secrets from fork PRs, which covers forks only. Needed:
- require code-owner review for .github/workflows/ (CODEOWNERS)
- never use pull_request_target with fork code
- pin third-party Actions to a commit SHA
- use a SonarCloud token limited to project analysis, and a Snyk service-account token
- rotate both tokens if one is ever exposed

threats.title: Scan tokens exfiltrated by a collaborator's PR
threats.description: Who: anyone with write access, or a stolen collaborator account (fork PRs do not receive secrets). How: a PR from a branch in this repo changes a workflow or a script the job runs so it sends SONAR_TOKEN / SNYK_TOKEN to an outside server (GitHub masks secrets in logs, so exfiltration goes over the network). Harmed: the vulnerability lists in SonarCloud/Snyk (an attack roadmap) and the gates themselves (issues marked accepted). [Reasoned by the student 2026-11-08.]
threats.mitigation: Prevent: require code-owner review on /.github/ (CODEOWNERS exists but the require-pr ruleset needs 0 approvals, so it is not enforced); least-privilege tokens (Sonar 'Execute Analysis' only); rotate. Detect: alert on workflow-file changes.

threats.title: Signing depends on Sigstore being available
threats.description: Who: none needed - an outage. How: keyless cosign signing needs Fulcio and Rekor online; if they are down, the release job fails. Harmed: releases stop (safe failure: nothing unsigned ships).
threats.mitigation: Accepted: fail closed is the right behaviour; retry on the next run. Note it in the runbook.

threats.title: Part of the deploy token printed into public Actions logs
threats.description:
Who: anyone on the internet. Actions logs on a public repo are public, kept 90 days by default.
How: a step prints part of the token, e.g. echo "${DEPLOY_TOKEN:0:6}..." to check it's set. GitHub only masks the exact full secret, so a piece or an encoded version prints in plain text. [Replace with the exact line from the workflow.]
Harmed: the visible part reveals the token type, cuts down guessing, and can be combined with other leaks into the full token, which can deploy any image to production, roll back, or take the service down.
threats.mitigation: Remove the line; never print any part of a secret. Delete old run logs that contain it, then rotate DEPLOY_TOKEN. Keep the token only in the production environment's secrets, behind required reviewers. Longer term, replace it with OIDC so there is no stored token to leak.

threats.title: Consumer runs an image without checking its signature
threats.description: Who: anyone able to push a look-alike image or change a tag. How: images are signed and release.yml's verify job runs cosign verify, but the ECS task (aws-estate fargate-service main.tf:137) just pulls var.image - nothing checks the signature at deploy time. Harmed: production could run an unsigned or replaced image.
threats.mitigation: Prevent: deploy by digest (@sha256:...), not by tag; verify the cosign signature before deploy (a pipeline step, or admission control in J08 with Kyverno verifyImages). Ticket.
